title: Cerebral palsy, hereditary ataxia, Huntington's and anoxic brain damage
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's neurological condition (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for mobility and gait.

HPI
Pt is a 63-year-old female presenting for routine f/u of long-standing spastic diplegic cerebral palsy since birth. Pt reports stable condition with no acute changes in mobility or coordination. She continues to use forearm crutches for ambulation. Denies new falls, severe contractures, or increased pain in lower extremities. Reports adherence to current physical therapy regimen.

Medication List
1. Gabapentin 300mg BID
2. Baclofen 10mg TID
3. Vitamin D3 1000 IU daily

Review of Systems
Constitutional: No fever, chills, or weight changes.
Musculoskeletal: Chronic stiffness in lower extremities. No acute joint pain.
Neurological: No new tremors or weakness.
Skin: No breakdown or pressure sores.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History
Pt lives in a single-story home with her spouse. Retired. No tobacco use. Occasional social outings with crutches.

Family History
Mother: Hypertension.
Father: Type 2 Diabetes.
Siblings: No known chronic conditions.

Vitals
BP: 128/82
HR: 74 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Ht/Wt: 5'4", 155 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 5.4%
eGFR: >90 mL/min
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L

Exam
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in no acute distress.
Respiratory: CTAB.
Musculoskeletal: Spastic diplegic gait noted. Good strength in upper extremities. Moderate hypertonicity in bilateral lower extremities. No new skin breakdown over heels.
Neurological: Normal sensation to light touch. Reflexes 3+ in lower extremities.

Assessment
1. Spastic diplegic cerebral palsy. Stable.

Plan
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Continue PT for gait maintenance and stretching.
3. F/u in 6 months or as needed for acute issues.

Electronically signed,
T. Haddad, NP
